title: process: boundary register — every design note names the edges it touches and the tests that pin them
body:
## Problem (the owner's observation, taken seriously)

"Each time we solve an issue we break something and a new issue comes out — we must understand the relationship between entities and know what is going to break."

Forensics over the whole tracker (done 2026-11-03, A/B worktrees included) say the perception is precise but the mechanism is not regression:

- **Zero of the campaign issues #23–#30 were caused by a previous fix.** Proof for the latest: #30's flush-race distribution is IDENTICAL at pre-#27 (`93ff6ba`) and pre-#28 (`5ca7f99`) — the resplit fixes did not cause it; the nightly simply exposed it for the first time.
- **Every defect in project history lived at an entity BOUNDARY**, under timing or semantics owned by the other side: server wire semantics (#24, `"`, 409 realign, #30 flush), cross-entity orchestration (#25 lone-vote eviction, #26 Finishing-cancel, #27 orphaned policy), measurement reality (#23 NameError, #28 64 KB bursts vs the server's 30 s idle timeout, #29 link-speed races), or state truth (#15 unknown-state resurrection).
- The true regressions were all process slips (defects 8–11, two pipe-masked gate exits) — each institutionalized a non-bypassable guard.

The predictive map ("what gonna break = whichever edge the next probe touches") currently lives in chat history. Chat is not memory — GitHub is. This issue turns the map into a checkable repo artifact.

## Design note (process change — docs + templates only, zero engine code)

1. **`docs/08_Boundary_Register.md`** — the register:
   - entity map re-derived from real `use crate::` edges (grep command included so it can be re-verified any session);
   - the seam table: edge → what it owns → every defect that lived there → the test(s) that now pin it;
   - the predictive rule and the maintenance rule (register row added/updated in the same commit as any change to an edge).
2. **docs/05 step 2 gains three mandatory design-note fields** for every non-trivial issue:
   (a) entities touched, (b) edges at risk, (c) the pinning test per at-risk edge — an unpinned edge means a new test in the same issue, not a promise.
3. **Issue templates gain a Boundary register field** so the audit happens at filing time, not after the break.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/08_Boundary_Register.md` exists; its seam table covers EVERY defect to date with the pinning test cited
- [ ] the entity map in docs/08 matches a fresh `use crate::` grep (shown in the issue on close)
- [ ] docs/05 loop step 2 + Rules of engagement updated
- [ ] feature.yml + bug.yml carry the field; both parse with `yaml.safe_load`
- [ ] committed-tree gate green (docs-only change, gate still runs — discipline is the point)

## Refs

#30 (A/B forensics), docs/05_Engineering_Process.md, STATUS.md §7 architecture map, defect audit trail §5.
